note.value: Palimpsest folios with underwriting in Syriac Estrangela: ff. 123–128, 149–166.

Five series of quire signatures are present reflecting the condition of the manuscript during different stages of its history. The oldest series of quire signatured can be found written in old Syriac numerals in the inner edge of a bottom margin of the quire’s first folio recto side and running until quire XX. The second series features in the middle of a bottom margin of the quire’s first folio recto side and corresponds to the original series. The third series marked in Arabic at the outer edge of the upper margin of the quire’s first folio recto side also corresponds to the original series but most probably was marked after the repair, when the codex received additional quires; the signatures for quires XI–XXIII are noticeable, others must have been cut during trimming. The fourth series of quire signatures was added after the codex was supplemented by liturgical indices and reached 25 quires; these signatures were written vertically in the bottom of the first and last pages of a quire. The fifth series was provided in Greek (signatures for quires V–XXV are at present visible) at the center of the upper margin of the quire’s first folio recto side and corresponds to the previous one.

Binding in fair condition. Relatively recent; leather on wood showing signs of repair; metal studs (some missing) on front and back and along edges; remnants of clasps (four total, two for edge and one each at top and bottom).

The manuscript underwent several repairs throughout its history until the 13th century. To one of the earliest repairs belong ff. 45–46, when the scribe tried to reproduce the layout of the original codex. Somewhat later, in Syriac Chalcedonian milieu, other missing parts were restored (ff. 123–128, 153–166). Most probably on another occasion, but also in Syriac Chalcedonian milieu, were added ff. 1–10, 17–41. Later on, ff. 149–152 were supplied on paper. In 1260 on Mount Sinai, additional paper folios were added.
Palimpsest folios with underwriting in Syriac Estrangela: ff. 123–128, 149–166.
